source: Ya'aqov - The Hebrew Epistle of James v2.0
note: Hebrew has 26 verses; Greek has 27. Greek v21 is entirely absent from the Hebrew. Hebrew vv21-26 = Greek vv22-27.

verses.translation: Ya'aqov{H3290}, servant{H5650} of YHWH{H3068} and of the Lord{H113} Yeshua the Mashiach{H4899}, to the twelve{H8147}{H6240} tribes{H7626} who are scattered{H6327} in all{H3605} the places{H4725}: joy{H8057} beforehand.

one_way_hebrew: Uses simchah (joy, H8057) as the greeting. Greek has chairein, a stock epistolary formula meaning greetings. The Hebrew is a concrete declaration: Joy! A back-translator from Greek would use shalom, not simchah.
Uses YHWH (H3068) where Greek has theou (God). Throughout the epistle, Hebrew uses the divine name where Greek has the generic theos.
Uses mefuzarim (scattered, H6327). Greek has en te diaspora (in the dispersion). Hebrew uses a native verb; Greek uses a technical term.
greek_deviations: Hebrew has mikkodem (beforehand) after simchah, absent from Greek.
Hebrew: in all the places. Greek: in the dispersion.
translation_notes: The greeting simchah mikkodem sets the thematic tone; joy recurs at the trial (v2) and characterizes the law itself (v24, dat hasimchah).

verses.translation: My brothers{H251} beloved{H157}, count{H2803} this for joy{H8057} if you fall{H5307} into trial{H5254}.

one_way_hebrew: Uses noflim (fall, H5307). Greek has peripesete (encounter). The Hebrew verb is more direct and physical.
greek_deviations: Greek adds various trials. Hebrew simply says trial (singular).

verses.translation: And know{H3045} that your faith{H530}, if it is complete{H8003}, produces endurance{H5450}.

one_way_hebrew: Hebrew says your faith, if it is COMPLETE (shelemah, H8003), produces endurance. Greek says the TESTING of your faith produces patience. Different mechanism: Hebrew conditions on faith quality; Greek conditions on the testing process.

Uses sivlut (endurance/bearing, H5450 from saval). This is the word for burden-bearing of Israelite slaves in Egypt (Ex 1:11, 6:6-7). Greek has hupomone (patience). No back-translator would choose the Exodus slavery word.
greek_deviations: Hebrew: complete faith produces endurance. Greek: testing of faith produces patience.

verses.translation: But the endurance{H5450} must be to the end{H5490}, so that you shall be in fullness and not lack{H2637} any thing{H1697} from you.

greek_deviations: Hebrew: in fullness (one concept). Greek: perfect and complete (two words).
translation_notes: Milu'ah (fullness) shares the root of milu'im (priestly ordination offerings, Ex 29:22, Lev 8:28).

verses.translation: But if there is one{H259} among you who lacks{H2637} wisdom{H2451}, he must pray{H6419} from YHWH{H3068} who gives{H5414} to every{H3605} man{H120}, and he will also give{H5414} to him.

one_way_hebrew: Uses litpallel (to pray, H6419, hitpael of palal), reflexive self-examination. Greek has aiteito (let him ask), a simple request.
greek_deviations: Greek adds without reproach, absent from Hebrew.
Hebrew: from YHWH. Greek: from God.

verses.translation: But he must pray{H6419} in faith{H530} and not in doubt, for whoever is in doubt, he is like scales{H3976} upon the sea{H3220}.

one_way_hebrew: CRITICAL: Uses moznayim (scales/balance, H3976). Greek has a wave of the sea driven by wind. Entirely different imagery! The Hebrew pictures a set of scales placed on the sea, forever tipping one way then the other. A back-translator from Greek would write gal hayam (wave of the sea), NEVER the scales word moznayim. Connects to Job 6:2 and Proverbs 16:11.
greek_deviations: Hebrew: like scales upon the sea (static balance). Greek: like a wave of the sea driven by wind (dynamic wave).

verses.translation: And this man{H120} must not think{H2803} that he shall receive any thing{H1697} from the Lord{H113}.
And a doubting master{H1167} is without knowledge{H1847} in all{H3605} his ways{H1870}.

one_way_hebrew: Uses ba'al (H1167, master/possessor). Greek has aner dipsuchos (double-minded man). Ba'al means owner, lord, husband. No back-translator would choose ba'al.
Uses beli yedi'at (without knowledge). Greek akatastatos means unstable. Hebrew: ignorance; Greek: instability.
greek_deviations: Hebrew: a doubting master. Greek: a double-minded man.

verses.translation: But a brother{H251} who is lowly{H8217} may boast of his height{H1363}.

translation_notes: The shafal/govah contrast is a Hebrew word-pair (Isa 2:11, Ezek 17:24).

verses.translation: And the rich{H6223} must boast of his lowliness{H8216}, for like a flower{H6731} of the field{H7704} he shall wither{H3001}.

one_way_hebrew: Uses ketsits hasadeh (flower of the field), echoing Isaiah 40:6 verbatim. Greek has flower of grass (anthos chortou). Hebrew preserves Isaiah's exact phrase; Greek changes field to grass.
greek_deviations: Hebrew: flower of the field (Isaiah 40:6). Greek: flower of grass.
textual_notes: Isaiah 40:6-8: All flesh is grass and all its beauty like the flower of the field.

verses.translation: And like a flower{H6731} he goes out{H3318} and withers{H4135} and flees{H1272} like a shadow{H6738} and shall not stand{H5975}.

one_way_hebrew: CRITICAL: vayyivrach katsel velo ya'amod (flees like a shadow and does not stand) is from Job 14:2. Hebrew preserves BOTH halves of Job 14:2 (flower v10, shadow v11). Greek has in his journeys he shall wither, with no shadow imagery. A back-translator from Greek would never import Job 14:2.
greek_deviations: Hebrew: flees like a shadow (Job 14:2). Greek: shall wither in his pursuits. No shadow in Greek.
textual_notes: Job 14:1-2: Man born of woman comes out like a flower and withers; he flees like a shadow and does not stand.

verses.translation: And blessed{H835} is the mortal{H582} whom Eloah{H433} reproves{H3198} -- and the discipline{H4148} of Shaddai{H7706} do not despise{H3988} -- for after the sufferings you shall receive the crown{H3804} of life{H2416} that YHWH{H3068} promises to those who love{H157} him.

one_way_hebrew: STRONGEST ONE-WAY MARKER: First half is VERBATIM Job 5:17: ashrei enosh yokichenu Eloah umusar Shaddai al tim'as. Uses three Job-signature words: enosh (mortal, H582, 42x in Job), Eloah (H433, 41x in Job out of 57 OT total), Shaddai (H7706, 31x in Job out of 48 OT total). Greek James 1:12 says Blessed is the man who endures temptation with NO Job connection. No translator going Greek-to-Hebrew would compose a verbatim Job 5:17 quotation.
Uses keter (crown, H3804), the royal crown (Esther 1:11, 2:17). Greek has stephanon (athletic wreath). Different types of crown.
greek_deviations: The entire Job 5:17 quote is ABSENT from Greek.
Hebrew: keter (royal crown). Greek: stephanos (athletic wreath).
translation_notes: Mortal for enosh emphasizes frailty (from root meaning to be weak/sick).
Eloah and Shaddai preserved as distinct divine titles of Job and the patriarchal tradition (Gen 17:1, Ex 6:3).
textual_notes: Job 5:17 is spoken by Eliphaz. James recontextualizes his partial wisdom as complete gospel truth, promising the crown of life after suffering.

verses.translation: And let not one{H259} say{H559} if a trial comes{H935} upon him, this comes from YHWH{H3068}, for YHWH{H3068} does not test{H5254} man{H120} for evil{H7451}, and he is not tested by anyone.

one_way_hebrew: Hebrew: YHWH does not test man for evil (purpose statement). Greek: God cannot be tempted by evil (nature statement). Different claims.
greek_deviations: Hebrew uses YHWH twice. Greek uses theos.

verses.translation: But every{H3605} one{H259} is tested{H5254} if his desire{H8378} overcomes{H5329} him.

one_way_hebrew: Uses menatseach (overcomes, H5329 natsach), the root of the Psalm superscription lamenatseach (55 times). Greek says drawn away and enticed (passive luring). Hebrew is ACTIVE: desire CONQUERS the person.
greek_deviations: Hebrew: desire overcomes (active). Greek: drawn away and enticed (passive).

verses.translation: And afterward, if desire{H8378} is received, it produces sin{H2399}; but sin{H2399}, if it is completed{H3615}, produces death{H4194}.

greek_deviations: Greek uses birth imagery (desire conceived gives birth to sin). Hebrew uses causal language: desire produces sin. No birth metaphor in Hebrew.

verses.translation: Do not go astray{H8582}, brothers{H251} beloved{H157}.

one_way_hebrew: Uses tit'u (go astray, H8582 ta'ah), the OT verb for wandering like lost sheep (Ps 119:176, Isa 53:6). Greek planasthe means be deceived. Hebrew: moral WANDERING; Greek: being MISLED.

verses.translation: Every{H3605} good{H2896} gift{H4979} comes from above{H4605}, from the light{H216} of the Father{H1}, and beside{H681} him there is no exchange or change from light{H216} and from darkness{H2822}.

one_way_hebrew: Uses or/choshekh (light/darkness, H216/H2822), Genesis 1:3-4 creation vocabulary. Greek says no variation or shadow of turning (abstract astronomical language). Hebrew uses concrete primordial imagery.
Uses etslo (beside him, H681 etsel), the unusual spatial proximity word, same as Rev 21:3.
greek_deviations: Hebrew: no exchange from light and from darkness (concrete). Greek: no variation or shadow of turning (astronomical).
textual_notes: Genesis 1:3-4: God separated between the light (or) and the darkness (choshekh).

verses.translation: And he showed{H7200} us according to his will{H7522}, by the word{H1697} of truth{H571}, that we are firstfruits{H1061} of his creation{H1254}.

one_way_hebrew: Uses her'ah (showed, H7200). Greek has apekyesen (birthed). Hebrew: God SHOWED us; Greek: God BIRTHED us.
Uses bikkurim (firstfruits, H1061), the Temple/agricultural offering term (Ex 23:19, Lev 23:17), tied to Shavuot.
greek_deviations: Hebrew: he showed us (revelation). Greek: he brought us forth (generation).
translation_notes: The bikkurim connect to Shavuot; the community born at Pentecost is the firstfruits offering.

verses.translation: For this reason, brothers{H251} beloved{H157}, every{H3605} son{H1121} of man{H120} must be swift to hear{H8085} but not to speak{H1696} and not to anger{H639}.

one_way_hebrew: Uses benei adam (sons of man/Adam, H1121/H120). Greek has every man. The Hebrew collective connects to the creation narrative.
translation_notes: Echoes Ecclesiastes 5:1-2: Be not rash with your mouth, let your words be few.

verses.translation: For the anger{H639} of the sons{H1121} of man{H120} does not produce what is good{H2896} before{H6440} YHWH{H3068}.

one_way_hebrew: Uses lifnei YHWH (before the face of YHWH). Greek: does not produce the righteousness of God. Hebrew: what is GOOD (moral quality). Greek: RIGHTEOUSNESS (legal standing).
greek_deviations: Hebrew: good before YHWH. Greek: the righteousness of God.

verses.translation: But be from those who do{H6213} the word{H1697} and not from the hearers{H8085} only, who by themselves deceive{H7411} you.

textual_notes: This is Hebrew v21 = Greek v22. Greek 1:21 (lay aside all filthiness and receive with meekness the implanted word, able to save your souls) is ENTIRELY ABSENT from the Hebrew.

verses.translation: For if one{H259} is a hearer{H8085} of the word{H1697} and does not do{H6213} it, he is like a man{H376} who sees{H7200} himself in the mirrors{H4759} of the serving-women{H6633}.

one_way_hebrew: AMONG THE STRONGEST ONE-WAY MARKERS: Uses mar'ot hatsov'ot (mirrors of the serving-women). This phrase appears ONLY in Exodus 38:8, describing bronze mirrors donated by women who served at the Tent of Meeting, melted into the priestly washing basin (laver). Greek has merely in a mirror (generic). NO back-translator would produce this Tabernacle reference. The metaphor: the man gazes into mirrors that should have become the laver of purification; he sees but never washes, never enters service.
greek_deviations: Hebrew: mirrors of the serving-women (plural, Tabernacle). Greek: a mirror (singular, generic).
translation_notes: Theological arc: mirrors for seeing; laver for washing/purification and priestly service. Hearing without doing is using the mirror but refusing the laver.
textual_notes: Exodus 38:8: The women's mirrors were melted into the kiyyor (laver) for priestly washing (Ex 30:17-21).

verses.translation: Since after he saw{H7200} himself, he goes{H1980} from it and forgets{H7911} what he saw{H7200}.

But whoever sees{H7200} in fullness into the law{H1881} of joy{H8057} and upholds{H6965} it, and does not forget{H7911} what he heard{H8085}, but does{H6213} it -- he shall be holy{H6918} in all{H3605} his deeds{H4639}.

one_way_hebrew: CRITICAL: dat hasimchah (the law of joy, H1881/H8057). Greek: the perfect law of liberty/freedom. Hebrew: JOY; Greek: FREEDOM. The law of joy connects to the greeting simchah (v1) and joy in trials (v2). No back-translator from liberty would substitute joy.
Uses dat (H1881) not torah for law. The author distinguishes dat (binding decree, Esther/Daniel) from torah (instruction). Greek has only nomos. This distinction cannot arise by back-translation.
Uses yihyeh kadosh (shall be HOLY, H6918). Greek: shall be BLESSED. Holiness (Lev 19:2) vs. blessedness. A back-translator would write ashrei, not kadosh.
greek_deviations: Hebrew: law of joy. Greek: perfect law of liberty.
Hebrew: shall be holy. Greek: shall be blessed.
translation_notes: Law of joy: the dat is not a burden but a source of joy. Psalm 19:8: The precepts of YHWH are right, rejoicing the heart.

verses.translation: But if one{H259} among you thinks to himself that he serves{H5647} YHWH{H3068} and does not guard{H8104} his tongue{H3956} with a bridle{H7448}, but entices{H5496} his heart{H3824} -- this service of YHWH{H3068} is not good{H2896}.

one_way_hebrew: CRITICAL: Uses she'irut (service, from sharat H8334, priestly/Tabernacle service). Greek has threskeia (religion). Hebrew is concrete ministerial SERVICE, not abstract religion. A back-translator from threskeia would use avodah or dat, not she'irut.
Uses hissit (enticed, H5496 sut), the verb for the adversary inciting David (1 Chr 21:1) and regarding Job (Job 2:3). Greek apaton means deceiving.
Uses resen (bridle, H7448), connecting to horse/bridle imagery in 3:3. A structural thread through the epistle.
greek_deviations: Hebrew: she'irut (service). Greek: threskeia (religion).
Hebrew: not good. Greek: worthless (mataios).
translation_notes: Service for she'irut captures priestly/ministerial meaning.

verses.translation: And the pure{H2889} service, without deficiency, before{H6440} YHWH{H3068} the Father{H1} -- this is he who goes{H1980} to visit{H1239} the orphans{H3490} and the widows{H490} in their distresses.

one_way_hebrew: Again uses she'irut (service, not religion). Pure service is defined solely by visiting orphans and widows.
greek_deviations: Hebrew ends here. Greek ADDS and to keep oneself unspotted from the world. Hebrew defines pure service solely as visiting orphans and widows.
translation_notes: tahor (H2889) is the Levitical purity term (Lev 11-15).
textual_notes: Deuteronomy 10:18, 14:29, 24:17 and Isaiah 1:17 mandate care for orphans and widows.

chapter_notes.summary: James 1 in Hebrew contains at least 10 clear one-way translation markers. The most extraordinary is the VERBATIM quotation of Job 5:17 in verse 12, using Job's three signature words (enosh, Eloah, Shaddai) completely absent from the Greek. The mar'ot hatsov'ot (mirrors of the serving-women, v22) from Exodus 38:8 is equally decisive. The dat hasimchah (law of joy, v24) reveals a fundamentally different framework from Greek's perfect law of liberty, with simchah (joy) as the epistle's keynote. Additional markers: moznayim (scales, v6) vs Greek wave; Job 14:2 shadow imagery (v11); or/choshekh creation vocabulary (v17) vs Greek astronomical abstraction; sivlut (Exodus burden-bearing, v3) vs patience; she'irut (priestly service, vv25-26) vs religion. YHWH appears throughout where Greek has God, and Greek v21 has no Hebrew counterpart.
